target_state: implemented staging handoff. The 68-instruction body was re-derived from the image bytes for this package, the three jump tables were READ OUT OF THE IMAGE at their own bases (0x00dd08f4, 0x00dd0908, 0x00dd0928) and transcribed word for word, and all three direct callees were read out of the image to fix their conventions, their argument counts and their argument order -- which turned up the finding that 0x004eb930's SECOND argument is the word 0x00dd0871 pushed for 0x00401090, which 0x00401090 never consumed. Outcome: the body is fully reconstructed, including the two-level pointer chase, the transposed pair of inner jump tables, the unsigned guards, and the two wrapping conditional stores. No member is named, no stored value is named, and three questions are left open.

intended_paths.status: staging-only handoff; no canonical path is claimed and no other package's files were touched

implementation.argument_surface: a hidden receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x00dd07f1 and used for every receiver access afterwards. ZERO ordinary stack arguments on all seven exits: the frame is four bytes deep from the single PUSH ESI at 0x00dd07f0, the only other ESP movement in the whole body is 0x00dd0871's PUSH EAX, 0x00dd087e's PUSH EAX and 0x00dd0887's ADD ESP,0x8, which are the two call arguments and their removal, and all seven return sites are a bare C3 with no immediate
implementation.return_type_choice: OPTION (b) of the two the contract allows, and chosen deliberately. The machine-derived record's return_semantics is the machine-vocabulary phrase 'unclassified_in_EAX' and the derived projection's RT2 classifies the last EAX write as aggregate_unknown; no C++ type can equal that string, so the check is a WARN whatever this package writes. Declaring void is a claim about the LISTING and it is true of the listing: EAX is written on every one of the seven exits and never with the same kind of thing twice -- it holds a pointer on the null-link and -2 paths, -1 on the -3 path, a jump-table index on four paths, and a callee's return on the three-callee path -- and the function's entire output is the dword at receiver+0x8c. Ghidra's own decompilation of the body declares `void __fastcall FUN_00dd07f0(int param_1)` and the persisted prototype is `undefined FUN_00dd07f0(void)`, so the decompiler agrees. No typedef named after the machine phrase was invented, which would be a validator hack. The disagreement is recorded in unresolved_questions item 1.
implementation.receiver_model: a struct of 0x9c opaque bytes with NO named member, because the machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only (SUPPORTED) and enumerates only displacements [132, 136, 140, 152] = 0x84, 0x88, 0x8c, 0x98. Every access goes through word_at(base + displacement) or pointer_at() with the displacement as a named constexpr, and the .cpp static_asserts each literal displacement against the header's named constant. The 0x9c length is this body's REACH, not a claim about the object: 0x98 + 4 is the last byte it loads
implementation.dispatch_model: none in the virtual sense, and none declared. The body has three indirect transfers and all three are switch dispatches over tables the body itself addresses: 0x00dd084b `JMP [ECX*0x4+0x00dd08f4]`, 0x00dd085b `JMP [EAX*0x4+0x00dd0908]` and 0x00dd08a3 `JMP [EAX*0x4+0x00dd0928]`. abi_derived.dispatch records vtable_shaped_loads 0 and call_offsets []; the record's four associated data tables (0x0147ca30, 0x0147ca70, 0x0147caf8, 0x0147cc14) and its three inbound xrefs (0x0147cabc, 0x0147cb84, 0x0147cc74) establish no slot boundary here, so no slot index and no slot displacement is declared anywhere in this package
implementation.dependency_note: all three direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the model test, which never defines the reconstructed body itself

function_extent.return_site: seven, all bare RET (byte C3): 0x00dd0815, 0x00dd0836, 0x00dd086d, 0x00dd089e, 0x00dd08b5, 0x00dd08c1, 0x00dd08cd, and the shared 0x00dd08f1 reached by five no-write paths and one write path. No immediate on any of them
function_extent.listing_reexported: objdump -D -b binary -m i386 -M intel --adjust-vma=0x00dd07f0 over the 0x14c bytes of SPORE/SporeBin/SporeApp.exe at file offset 0x9c07f0 (RVA 0x9d07f0, .text base 0x401000 at file offset 0xfcb000) reproduces the 68 committed instructions at the same addresses with the same lengths, branch targets and operand displacements. observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: ESI -- `MOV ESI,ECX` at 0x00dd07f1, and every receiver access afterwards names ESI (0x00dd07f3, 0x00dd080a, 0x00dd0816, 0x00dd082b, 0x00dd0837, 0x00dd0862, 0x00dd086e, 0x00dd0897, 0x00dd08aa, 0x00dd08b6, 0x00dd08c2, 0x00dd08ce, 0x00dd08ea). ECX is REUSED twice as scratch: at 0x00dd0801 it takes the level-2 pointer and at 0x00dd0837 it takes the kind word. This is why the machine-derived receiver record reports register ECX with shape R-ALIAS: the base register it saw the receiver in is not the base register the listing's own receiver operands name, so a naive ECX-only displacement scan of the listing finds nothing in bounds
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_note: none. The frame is four bytes deep from the single PUSH ESI at 0x00dd07f0; the only other ESP movement in the 68 instructions is 0x00dd0871's PUSH EAX, 0x00dd087e's PUSH EAX and 0x00dd0887's ADD ESP,0x8, which are the two call arguments and their removal. No instruction in the 68 reads a stack slot, so there is no parameter of any kind
observed_original_abi.stack_cleanup_sites: none in this body. 0x00dd0887's ADD ESP,0x8 is the caller-side drop of the two words pushed at 0x00dd0871 and 0x00dd087e, not an argument of this body
observed_original_abi.return_semantics_machine: EAX is written on every one of the seven exits and by nothing that a caller could use: the level-1 pointer (0x00dd07f3) on the null-link and -2 paths, the sentinel comparison's own -1 (0x00dd0823) on the -3 path, the jump-table index (0x00dd0843, 0x00dd0852, 0x00dd089f) on four paths, and 0x004eb930's byte (0x00dd087f) on the three-callee path. Five DIFFERENT kinds of value, so there is no width and no C type that fits all of them
observed_original_abi.ghidra_prototype: undefined FUN_00dd07f0(void), parameter_count 0, return_type undefined, return_type_resolved false; its decompilation declares `void __fastcall FUN_00dd07f0(int param_1)`
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: Ghidra reports __fastcall because a one-argument x86-32 member function and a hidden-this function are indistinguishable to it. The record disagrees (conventions.calling_convention '__thiscall', candidate set [__thiscall, __fastcall], confidence INFERRED) and the listing settles it: the body's only EDX use is the guard constant 0x00dd083e sets for its own compares, which it never passes to anything, so the second fastcall register is unused. __thiscall is the model. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved by picking the convenient answer
observed_original_abi.dispatch: abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 3, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0. All three indirect transfers are the switch JMPs listed above, over tables in the body's own .text. The model declares no slot boundary and the source span was audited for the five slot-boundary tokens the check looks for (load_slot, object_slot, shell_slot, vtable, slot[) and contains none of them in code -- the decoded target addresses are named kTargetStore0, kTargetBareStore, kTargetBareEpilogue and so on for exactly that reason
observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: each fixed by the callee's own bytes, read from the image for this package. 0x00401090 is 10 bytes ending in a bare C3 at 0x00401099 and reads no stack slot and no argument register, so cdecl with ZERO arguments -- and it IGNORES the word 0x00dd0871 pushed for it. 0x004df400 is 19 bytes ending in a bare C3 at 0x004df412; it stores ECX at 0x004df404 and reloads it at 0x004df407 and reads no [ebp+0x8], so __thiscall with the receiver in ECX and no stack argument. 0x004eb930 is 0x43 bytes ending in a bare C3 at 0x004eb972 and reads BOTH [ebp+0x8] and [ebp+0xc], so cdecl with TWO four-byte stack arguments
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: ABI_INFERRED (abi_derived.verdict = ABI_INFERRED, completeness = CORE_RESOLVED, conventions.confidence = INFERRED, parse {declared_count 68, unparsed 0, degraded false})

mechanics.body_shape: chase two pointers out of one dword of the receiver; refuse twice on what is behind them; then write ONE dword of the receiver, receiver+0x8c, with a small code chosen by a two-level switch over the receiver's kind word at +0x84 and the record's sub-state word at record+0x20. Five of the seven exits write nothing at all

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 68 instructions. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; 0x00dd07f0's PUSH ESI makes it -4; nothing touches ESP for 33 instructions; 0x00dd0871's PUSH EAX makes it -8; 0x00dd0872's CALL 0x00401090 does not change it, because that callee's bare C3 removes only the return address; 0x00dd0879's CALL 0x004df400 does not either; 0x00dd087e's PUSH EAX makes it -12; 0x00dd087f's CALL 0x004eb930 does not; 0x00dd0887's ADD ESP,0x8 takes it back to -4; and each of the eight POP ESI instructions returns it to 0 before its RET
frame_resolution.corroboration: three agreements. (1) abi_derived.cleanup is {bytes 0, side caller, evidence 'ret with no immediate, no stack reads'} and abi_derived.abi lists no stack_arguments entry. (2) all eight return sites are a bare C3 with no immediate, read out of the image. (3) the three callees' own terminators are bare C3, which is what forces 0x00dd0887 to exist at all

slots.entry-12: the word pushed at 0x00dd087e for 0x004eb930: 0x004df400's return, removed by 0x00dd0887
slots.entry-8: the word pushed at 0x00dd0871: LEA EAX,[ESI+0x4], i.e. receiver+4. 0x00401090 never reads it, and because that callee's RET is bare it is STILL THERE at 0x00dd087f and becomes 0x004eb930's SECOND argument
slots.ordinary_arguments: none -- the receiver is the hidden this in ECX and nothing else is passed to THIS body

receiver_displacement.note: the body's COMPLETE memory surface on the receiver. Four displacements, three reads and nine writes, and those are the four the machine-derived receiver record enumerates: abi_derived.receiver is {register ECX, offsets [132, 136, 140, 152], max_offset 152, written_through 9, shape R-ALIAS, bounds_only true}
receiver_displacement.0x84: read ONCE, at 0x00dd0837 `MOV ECX,[ESI+0x84]`, and it is the outer switch's index after 0x00dd083d's DEC. No other instruction touches this displacement
receiver_displacement.0x88: read ONCE, at 0x00dd08ce `MOV EDX,[ESI+0x88]`, on the tag arm only. The model test proves the read is confined there by driving every other (kind, sub-state) pair with the tag word at two different values and requiring the answer not to move
receiver_displacement.0x8c: written at NINE sites and read by no instruction of this body: 0x00dd080a, 0x00dd0816, 0x00dd082b, 0x00dd0862, 0x00dd0897, 0x00dd08aa, 0x00dd08b6, 0x00dd08c2, 0x00dd08ea
receiver_displacement.0x98: read ONCE, at 0x00dd07f3 `MOV EAX,[ESI+0x98]`, and it is the only word the body follows a pointer out of
receiver_displacement.0x04: an ADDRESS the body FORMS at 0x00dd086e `LEA EAX,[ESI+0x4]`, not a word it reads. The twelve bytes there are read by 0x004eb930, which is why this body's own reach on the receiver stops at 0x9b while the callee reads lower

two_level_chain.claim: the machine reads a LEVEL-1 pointer at receiver+0x98, a LEVEL-2 pointer at [level1+0xc], and then the words +0x10 and +0x20 of THAT. So there are exactly two indirections before the record's own fields, and every one of them is a single MOV in the listing
two_level_chain.no_null_test_on_level_2: 0x00dd07f9's TEST is on the LEVEL-1 pointer. Nothing in the 68 instructions tests the level-2 pointer, so the model does not either, and the test does not construct that case because it would fault rather than refute. Recorded as unresolved_questions item 3
two_level_chain.the_two_loads_of_the_same_word: 0x00dd0801 and 0x00dd0820 read the SAME dword of the SAME level-1 object. The model reads it once and reuses the value, which is a fact about the listing rather than an optimisation: no branch, no call and no store lies between the two loads on any path. A version that loaded it twice is not distinguishable from this one on any input this function can be given. Recorded as unresolved_questions item 4

jump_tables.note: read out of the image with read_memory at the three bases, which are themselves the memory operands of the JMPs that use them. Transcribed word for word into the header and asserted there and again in the model test

outer_base_0x00dd08f4.index: *(receiver+0x84) - 1, legal 0..4 (0x00dd083d DEC, 0x00dd083e MOV EDX,0x4, 0x00dd0843 CMP ECX,EDX, 0x00dd0845 JA)
outer_base_0x00dd08f4.guard_is_unsigned: yes. kind 0 gives an index of 0xffffffff, and 0x00dd0845's JA leaves the function through 0x00dd08f0 with the 3 from 0x00dd0816 still in place. A signed compare would have let it index out of bounds

entries.0: 0x00dd0852 -- the kind-1 arm: guard 0x00dd0852 CMP EAX,0x7 / 0x00dd0855 JA, then 0x00dd085b JMP [EAX*0x4+0x00dd0908]
entries.1: 0x00dd089f -- the shared other arm: guard 0x00dd089f CMP EAX,EDX with EDX still 4, then 0x00dd08a3 JMP [EAX*0x4+0x00dd0928]
entries.2: 0x00dd08f0 -- the bare `POP ESI / RET` epilogue, which writes NOTHING

kind_one_sub_base_0x00dd0908.guard_is_unsigned: yes, 0x00dd0855 JA against 7. This is the ONLY table with a bound other than 4, and that is why indices 6 and 7 exist

entries.4: 0x00dd08ce -- the top of the recomputing block, which falls into the same store at 0x00dd08ea

the_transposed_pair.claim: the two inner tables put the BARE STORE on OPPOSITE indices -- index 4 of the kind-1 table and index 3 of the other arm's table -- and that is the single easiest thing to transpose in this body
the_transposed_pair.why_the_two_differ: 0x00dd08ea is the STORE at the tail of the 0x00dd08ce block and 0x00dd08ce is the TOP of that block. So an index that lands on 0x00dd08ea skips the recomputation and stores whatever EDX already holds, while an index that lands on 0x00dd08ce recomputes from receiver+0x88 first. The two entries are NOT the same outcome
the_transposed_pair.the_leftover_value: EDX is set to 4 at 0x00dd083e, read but never written by 0x00dd0843's CMP, and untouched by both jump-table dispatches, so both bare stores write 4. The guard constant and a stored answer are the same register and the same immediate, which nothing in the listing separates
the_transposed_pair.test: case_b2 pins all sixteen (kind, sub-state) pairs of the two inner tables individually, and case_b5 plants 0x53dbcf1 as the tag word and requires kind 2 with sub-state 3 to answer 4 while kind 2 with sub-state 4 answers the tag arm's word

tag_arm.at: 0x00dd08ce..0x00dd08ea, reached only from index 4 of the 0x00dd0928 table
tag_arm.derivation: 0x00dd08d4 SUB EDX,0x53dbcf1 makes EDX = tag - 0x53dbcf1 (wrapping). 0x00dd08da NEG EDX sets CF to 1 exactly when its operand was non-zero, i.e. exactly when tag != 0x53dbcf1. 0x00dd08dc SBB EDX,EDX gives -CF, so 0 or 0xffffffff. 0x00dd08de AND 0x80000006 gives 0 or 0x80000006. 0x00dd08e4 ADD 0x7fffffff is UNCONDITIONAL, so the zero case falls into it and leaves the addend alone: 0x7fffffff
tag_arm.the_other_case_wraps: 0x80000006 + 0x7fffffff is 0x100000005, which truncates to 5 -- NOT to 0x80000005. A reconstruction that adds without truncating produces a nine-digit word here. This is the easiest error in the whole body and the model test pins the full 32-bit pattern on eight tag values

callee_arm.at: 0x00dd0884..0x00dd0897, reached only from indices 6 and 7 of the 0x00dd0908 table
callee_arm.derivation: 0x00dd0884 MOVZX ECX,AL zero-extends ONE byte. 0x00dd088a NEG and 0x00dd088c SBB turn that into 0 or 0xffffffff. 0x00dd088e AND 0x7ffffffa gives 0 or 0x7ffffffa. 0x00dd0894 ADD 0x5 is unconditional, so 0x7ffffffa + 5 = 0x7fffffff, or 0 + 5 = 5
callee_arm.one_byte_selection: a callee that returned 0x00000100 would read as FALSE here, because only AL is consumed. The model's declared return is bool for that reason

the_two_conditional_stores.the_symmetry_that_makes_a_transposition_: the two blocks produce the SAME two words, 0x7fffffff and 5, from OPPOSITE operand roles: here the MASK plus the addend yields the large one, where the tag arm's mask plus its addend yields the small one. A reconstruction that transposed the two blocks' constants would be right about every answer and wrong about why. The model test therefore pins the constants themselves (kTagArmSelectMask 0x80000006, kTagArmSelectAddend 0x7fffffff, kCalleeArmSelectMask 0x7ffffffa, kCalleeArmSelectAddend 5) and not only the answers
the_two_conditional_stores.test: case_b5 sweeps the tag arm over eight tag values including one below and one above the subtractand, 0, 0x7fffffff and 0x80000000, and asserts the answer is never 0x80000005. case_b6 drives both polarities of the comparison and asserts the same for the callee arm

value_table.note: the dword at receiver+0x8c after the call, for every input, read straight off the three tables

written.-3 (0xfffffffd): when *(record+0x20) == 0xffffffff, at 0x00dd082b, OVERWRITING the 3 that 0x00dd0816 just stored
written.0x7fffffff: the tag arm when *(receiver+0x88) == 0x53dbcf1, and the callee arm when the comparison came back true
written.0x00000005: the tag arm's other answer, and the callee arm's other answer
written.4: the bare store at 0x00dd08ea: sub-state 4 on the kind-1 table, sub-state 3 on the other arm's table

value_table.left_at_3: the null link's path leaves it alone entirely, and every other no-write path leaves 0x00dd0816's 3: kind 3, kind 0 or greater than 5, and an out-of-range sub-state on either arm
value_table.left_untouched: only the null-link exit at 0x00dd07fb and the -2 exit at 0x00dd0808 return without 0x00dd0816 having run; every other path writes the word at least once

mechanics.control_flow: exactly SIX conditional branches in the whole body, with targets inside the recovered 258-byte span: JZ 0x00dd08f0 at 0x00dd07fb (the null link), JNZ 0x00dd0816 at 0x00dd0808 (the record kind), JNZ 0x00dd0837 at 0x00dd0829 (the sub-state sentinel), and JA 0x00dd08f0 at 0x00dd0845, 0x00dd0855 and 0x00dd08a1 (the three unsigned index guards). FIVE of the six share the target 0x00dd08f0, the bare `POP ESI / RET` tail, which writes nothing -- so the most travelled destination in this function is the one that changes nothing. Plus THREE unconditional indirect transfers, the switch JMPs. No loop, no backward branch, no indirect CALL
mechanics.globals: none named by the body. No instruction in the 68 references a data-segment address: the jump-table bases 0x00dd08f4, 0x00dd0908 and 0x00dd0928 lie in the body's own .text immediately after it, and every other immediate is a small value. The one data word in the neighbourhood is 0x015d0c24, which 0x00401090's own body loads; it is recorded in the header as context, read by nothing in this model, and kept out of the source span so the GLOBALS check's evidenced-absence arm applies

direct_call_1.arguments: none that it reads. 0x00dd0871 pushes a word and this callee never looks at it: its entire body is `PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / MOV EAX,[0x015d0c24] / POP EBP / RET`
direct_call_1.cleanup: none on either side; the terminator is a bare C3 at 0x00401099, and the pushed word is STILL ON THE STACK afterwards
direct_call_1.return: the data word at 0x015d0c24, in EAX
direct_call_1.interpretation: an accessor for one global. The Ghidra name says otherwise -- the SDK signature takes an editor pointer -- but the bytes are the authority and the bytes read nothing. The name is kept for addressability and the discrepancy is recorded in unresolved_questions item 2

direct_call_2.convention: __thiscall, receiver in ECX and NO stack argument
direct_call_2.arguments: ECX, set by 0x00dd0877's `MOV ECX,EAX` to exactly what 0x00401090 returned. The callee stores ECX at 0x004df404 and reloads it at 0x004df407, so this is a receiver and not an argument
direct_call_2.cleanup: none; the terminator is a bare C3 at 0x004df412
direct_call_2.return: its receiver plus 0xa4, and nothing else -- the callee's whole body is that ADD
direct_call_2.callee_body_read_for_this_package: 0x004df400..0x004df412, 19 bytes. The interior is the callee's and is NOT modelled; only the signature and the 0xa4 displacement are used, and both are transcribed in the header
direct_call_2.test: case_c1 requires the receiver it is handed to be the previous callee's return and to be neither the object nor receiver+4, and requires its own return to be the receiver plus the shift

direct_call_3.arguments: TWO, and this is the finding the callee's own bytes produce. The callee reads [ebp+0x8] at 0x004eb934 and [ebp+0xc] at 0x004eb937, and dereferences both. Only ONE word is pushed between 0x00dd0872 and 0x00dd087f -- 0x00dd087e's PUSH EAX -- and 0x00401090's bare C3 removed only the return address, so at the call the stack holds [esp+4] = 0x004df400's return and [esp+8] = the word 0x00dd0871 pushed, which is receiver+4. So the callee's first argument is the shifted species-manager word and its second is receiver+4
direct_call_3.cleanup: caller-side, ADD ESP,0x8 at 0x00dd0887, which drops BOTH words -- 8 bytes for two calls that each pushed one
direct_call_3.return: one BYTE in AL: 1 only if [arg1+0], [arg1+4] and [arg1+8] all equal [arg2+0], [arg2+4] and [arg2+8]. 0x00dd0884's MOVZX ECX,AL consumes exactly that byte
direct_call_3.callee_body_read_for_this_package: 0x004eb930..0x004eb972, 0x43 bytes: three dword compares with three JNE short-circuits to a zero, and a one otherwise. The interior is NOT modelled; the twelve-byte width and the two-argument order are
direct_call_3.consequence_for_the_receiver_reach: the twelve bytes at receiver+4 that this callee reads lie INSIDE the receiver, so the object's real extent is at least receiver+0x10 -- but this body does not read them, and its own reach stops at 0x9b. The model does not widen its receiver for a callee's reads
direct_call_3.test: case_c1 records both argument addresses and requires them to be the shifted word and receiver+4 in that order; case_c2 requires the second one to be the very word 0x00dd0871 pushed; and the observer is deliberately ORDER-SENSITIVE, so swapping the two arguments changes the word the body STORES and not merely the recorded addresses

mechanics.callee_order: store 3 (0x00dd0816) -> 0x00401090 -> 0x004df400 -> 0x004eb930 -> drop two words (0x00dd0887) -> compute -> store the answer (0x00dd0897). Exactly one (kind, sub-state) pair of the reachable space -- kind 1 with sub-state 6 or 7 -- reaches any of the three
mechanics.write_ordering: there are two orderings and both are measured. The FORWARD one: 0x00dd0816's 3 precedes all three calls, so an observer planted at any of them reads 3 out of the result word (case_c3). The BACKWARD one: 0x00dd0897 is the last write on the callee path, so an observer that scribbles on the result word from inside the call loses (case_c5). And the -3 exit at 0x00dd082b overwrites the 3 rather than returning before it (case_a5)
mechanics.not_modelled: the interiors of all three callees; the 0xcc-equivalent hot-patch bytes at 0x00dd08f2 and the three tables themselves as data; the data word 0x015d0c24; the level-2 null case, which the listing does not test; and the MEANING of every word the body reads or writes

return_semantics.kind: nothing. The function is a writer
return_semantics.value: none. Every one of the seven exits leaves EAX holding a different KIND of thing -- a pointer, a sentinel, a jump-table index, or a callee's byte -- and the function's entire output is the dword at receiver+0x8c
return_semantics.signed_view: the stored words 0xfffffffe and 0xfffffffd are -2 and -3 as signed 32-bit words, which is how Ghidra's decompilation prints them. The model test compares on the unsigned bit pattern in every case, so the two views cannot disagree
return_semantics.ownership: nothing is acquired or released. The body reads three receiver words and one dword of a two-level chain, writes one receiver dword at up to nine sites, and allocates nothing
return_semantics.lifetime: nothing is frame-borne. The two pushed words are the callees' arguments and 0x00dd0887 removes them
return_semantics.why_void: EAX is written on every exit but never with the same kind of value twice, and the decompiler itself declares the function void. Declaring a C type would be asserting a width and an identity that the machine does not have
return_semantics.why_not_void_and_why_not_a_pointer: N/A -- this package declares void, and the reason is the opposite: there is no coherent EAX value to declare. See implementation.return_type_choice and unresolved_questions item 1

evidence.raw_bytes: not transcribed here; the 68-instruction listing above was re-derived from the image by objdump and matches the committed record instruction for instruction, and the three jump tables were read out of the image with read_memory at 0x00dd08f4, 0x00dd0908 and 0x00dd0928

evidence.decompiler_disagreements: three, and none of them touches a modelled point. (1) The convention: it says __fastcall where the record and the listing say __thiscall. (2) Its rendering of the tag arm: it prints the same arithmetic this package transcribes, and the value it computes -- 0x80000006 + 0x7fffffff truncated -- is 5, which the model reproduces. Its `iVar3 = 4` initial value IS the leftover EDX of the bare store, and its `case 3: break` on the other arm's table is exactly the 0x00dd08ea entry; reading that as a separate case storing a constant 4 would be a misreading of the decompiler, and the tables were read out of the image to settle it. validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit named checks, no framework and no external dependency. All three direct callees are defined in the test as observers that record their call count, their argument, the call order, the object as it stood at the moment of the call, the ESP they were entered at, and -- on instruction -- an option to rewrite the object from inside the call. Twenty-four cases in four groups. A: the two-level chain -- the null link, the record-kind equality at the right depth with nine wrong depths decoyed, the all-ones sub-state sentinel, the -3 store overwriting the 3, and a link to an all-zero record which is NOT the null exit. B: the switches -- a 4 x 13 x 13 x 2 sweep against an INDEPENDENT flat if/else oracle over (kind, sub-state, tag, comparison answer), the transposed-table decoy with all sixteen inner pairs pinned, both unsigned guards driven with 0, 6, 7, 8, 0x7fffffff, 0x80000000, 0xffffffff and 0xfffffffe, the tag arm over eight tag values, the callee arm in both polarities, and all eighteen transcribed table words against the bytes. C: the callees -- order, count, argument identity, argument order through an order-sensitive observer, write ordering measured at the moment of each call, which one leg of the table space ever calls, a mid-flight rewrite of the result word, and a mid-flight rewrite that cannot move the arm. D: measurements -- a raw thiscall trampoline with a poisoned decoy where a stack argument would be, a whole-object byte-for-byte compare, dword and byte decoys at every unmodelled receiver displacement, repeated and interleaved invocations, and the level-1 and level-2 neighbour decoys.
